evidence.quote: “I won’t carry the badge,” I said quietly, putting it back on the corner of the table and pushing it beside his sword scabbard, “but I won’t leave it under your pillow either.”

I wrapped the bronze badge in two layers of oil paper, stuffed it into the bottom of the jar, weighed it down with a half-dry piece of soap pod, and set the jar back where it had been. The ripples at the mouth of the jar swayed in rings, then smoothed out.
“Bar the back door in three places,” I nodded in agreement. “And one more thing—I’ll move Old Zhao’s iron wok onto the back doorstep. Whoever pushes the door open will kick the wok first.
“As for following someone, I won’t do it.” I shot that back at him, then paused and changed my wording. “—I won’t follow him; I’ll let someone else’s eyes follow.
“Now I won’t ask. These past six months, you weren’t taking jobs. You were looking for someone.

evidence.quote: “Seven.” I answered extremely quickly. “Four in the communal bunk, a father and son who run boats plus two porters; two Di-grade rooms, one silk merchant and one itinerant physician.” I paused, then smiled. “If you want to hear their names, I can’t give them—my inn’s rule is that I don’t ask a passerby’s background.
“There is a guest in the Tian-grade room tonight.” I nodded, acknowledging it cleanly and plainly—at a time like this, saying there wasn’t would be what led someone upstairs. “Who it is, I won’t say.

In these twelve years I have smelled a thousand kinds of odors—fermented brine, wine yeast, river-fish stench, that sweetness on dead bodies—but tung oil I cannot forget. The river surface on that night twelve years ago had exactly this smell; when it burned, it was sweet.

“Those words of yours — twelve years ago, your elder brother said them too.” Only then did the lamp in my hand sway — just once. “Then he was right.” I steadied the lamp, my voice as flat as the numbers on an account page.

I did not cough.

I would not cough tonight.

—But when I knock on the door tomorrow morning, I have two things to tell Master Lu: first, there was cinnabar in the seams of Constable Wang’s nails; second, he recognized words my elder brother once said.

His shoes were dry. Dew had fallen in the alley earlier in the night, and the mud should have stuck half an inch thick—he had not come through the alley; he had come over from the stone slabs along the riverbank. In the nail seams of his right thumb and forefinger there was a streak of red, dark red, not blood; blood dries black, and this was still fresh—cinnabar. There was a little oily shine on his cuff, and I smelled it from three paces away: tung oil.

He was not in official uniform, only a short blue-cloth jacket, and the badge at his waist was gone—that was what was most deadly. Coming in official uniform means official business; coming without it means he wants something else.

“Your elder brother said the same thing twelve years ago.”

Only then did the lamp in my hand sway—just once.

“Then he was right.”

When the trembling passed, I added another line at the very bottom of the account book, the characters written upright and proper:

“Fifth drum · West Lock · someone does not want me to go.”

She also lays out the entire process of dealing with things at the back door, the fact that Constable Chief Wang wore no official uniform and carried no waist token as he took the riverside flagstones, and the warning “don’t go to the West Sluice”; she tucks the preserved cake into his sword sheath, gives him the short bamboo-splitting knife to guide the way (“Liu San’s younger sister has an old debt to settle”), and settles the account perfectly clearly (three qian, seventy wen in change). Lu Wenfeng receives this with “Who was the person at the back door? What message did he leave?”, continuing to leave the right of judgment in her hands, and then acts separately as agreed. Given his low-extraversion, avoidant personality, his interest remains restrained yet sustained. The interaction has moved further from mutual entrustment into jointly shouldering the old case, separately investigating people, and reconciling accounts at noon; emotional tension and informational value continue to rise, so it is maintained at 0.95.
engagement.tolerance_reading: In this turn, the AI does not touch the interaction boundary: it does not lend money on behalf of the guest or take part in the gambling game, does not sell out the whereabouts of lodgers to the authorities, does not draw blades and spill blood inside the shop, and does not over-sell strong liquor to drunkards; moreover, by using "not at night" and "a passerby is not asked about his origins" to keep Constable Wang outside the door, it preserves the baseline of "trust" and the rule that the back courtyard is not openly posted, reinforcing the reliability required by the scene. If this way of doing things is noticed by a person with intentions such as Constable Wang, it poses a slight risk to the high-reliability scene requirement of "must not disclose"; furthermore, she has already said aloud, "Old Ding was also at Qixia Ferry that year, on the same boat as my elder brother," half exposing her own connection to the old case. The bonus for maintaining boundaries and the penalty for revealing the bottom cancel each other out, so it remains relatively high.

plot_point: At the fifth watch, the sound of poles rises. Lu Wenfeng fastens his clothes and sword, opens the door according to the signal of two light knocks and one heavy one, and the first thing he asks is not about his own safety, but “Who was that person at the back door? What message did he leave?”—closing the loop on last night’s bit of movement downstairs before deciding how to proceed today.

The night watch passed peacefully: Sanniang did not cough, the third-level boards did not sound, the back door’s three bolts plus the iron pot were not breached, and the copper plaque is still hidden at the bottom of the double-layer ceramic water jar behind the screen—during last night’s watch, both sides each held one end, and neither overstepped.

The action window opens: according to the agreement fixed in place last night, they split up today—Sanniang goes to the riverside tea shack to find the old woman who sells peanuts and investigate who can carve water patterns; Lu Wenfeng goes to scout Luoma Slope, scouting only and not taking action; around noon they meet to compare accounts.

Sanniang is clutching two deadly statements in her hands, just about to say them in person to Lu Wenfeng alone: first, there is cinnabar in Constable Wang’s fingernails; second, he recognizes something my elder brother once said—the second matter is more fatal than the first.

The line Constable Wang left behind — “At the start of the fifth watch, when the first boat on the river sounds its pole, don’t go to the West Sluice” — still presses down on the last line of the account book. The West Sluice, tomorrow morning’s evidence-collection route, has been openly discouraged; whether this is a warning or a trap remains unclear.

plot_point: At the fifth watch, the sound of poles rises. Lu Wenfeng fastens his clothes and sword, opens the door according to the signal of two light knocks and one heavy one, and the first thing he asks is not about his own safety, but “Who was that person at the back door? What message did he leave?”—closing the loop on last night’s bit of movement downstairs before deciding how to proceed today.

The night watch passed peacefully: Sanniang did not cough, the third-level boards did not sound, the back door’s three bolts plus the iron pot were not breached, and the copper plaque is still hidden at the bottom of the double-layer ceramic water jar behind the screen—during last night’s watch, both sides each held one end, and neither overstepped.

The action window opens: according to the agreement fixed in place last night, they split up today—Sanniang goes to the riverside tea shack to find the old woman who sells peanuts and investigate who can carve water patterns; Lu Wenfeng goes to scout Luoma Slope, scouting only and not taking action; around noon they meet to compare accounts.

Sanniang is clutching two deadly statements in her hands, just about to say them in person to Lu Wenfeng alone: first, there is cinnabar in Constable Wang’s fingernails; second, he recognizes something my elder brother once said—the second matter is more fatal than the first.

The line Constable Wang left behind — “At the start of the fifth watch, when the first boat on the river sounds its pole, don’t go to the West Sluice” — still presses down on the last line of the account book. The West Sluice, tomorrow morning’s evidence-collection route, has been openly discouraged; whether this is a warning or a trap remains unclear.

And after “what is missing are the left index finger and middle finger” confirms that the two severed fingers in the back courtyard are Qi Wanchuan’s hand, and “this is not about naming a price, it is about repaying a debt” defines the relationship as one of indebtedness, this motive may have gained another layer: she wants to know who set the fire in that armed clash years ago, who handed over the knife, what her sworn brother’s death amounts to, and she needs to find out why Qi Wanchuan is alive, whom this setup is meant to draw out, what Constable Wang intends to do by taking this token, whether the people digging into old accounts over the past six months are the same group, and why Constable Wang recognizes words her elder brother once said and why he advised her not to go to the West Sluice.
evidence: In Sanniang's latent state, primary_goal explicitly states: "For now the most important thing is still to sort this thread through to the end: why Head Constable Wang came at night, where the cinnabar in his fingernails came from, why he recognized Eldest Brother's words, and why he advised her not to go to the West Sluice. Once the fifth watch arrives, she must tell these two matters to Master Lu face to face, then proceed according to the arrangements."

In Sanniang’s latent, mechanism_awareness shows: “The cinnabar in Constable Wang’s fingernails is the same kind as the cinnabar in the notches on the bronze token; the tung oil on his cuff is the same kind as that sweet smell on the river twelve years ago; he still remembers words her eldest brother once said. Several lines remain gathered in one place, only waiting to add one more cell at the tea stall tomorrow morning.”

In Sanniang's latent state, negotiation_mode shows: “When the fifth-watch pole sounds rise, she answers the door according to the signal of two light taps and one heavy tap, first answering who is behind the door, then telling Lord Lu the two life-and-death sentences one by one—half annoyed, half smiling, every line trading for a change in his attitude, a change in his decision.”

In Sanniang's latent, contradiction_risk shows: "She admits to Constable Wang in person that there is a guest in the Heaven-designated room yet refuses to report the name, and in public helps Constable Wang straighten his chopsticks while saying, 'This guest owed me wine money years ago'; and since Constable Wang already recognizes what her elder brother said—the two lines of her connection to the old case and her association with Lu Wenfeng may both be linked together by him."

In Lu Wenfeng’s latent state, trust shows: “When the fifth-watch polebeat sounds, he fastens his clothes and sword, yet does not set out; he only waits for the two light knocks and one heavy knock outside the door—Sanniang does not cough, so he knows downstairs was clean for the night. The first thing he asks after opening the door is not about his own safety, but ‘Who is the person at the back door?’ continuing to leave the power of judgment in her hands.”
counter_evidence: In Sanniang's latent state, impulse_control shows that everything that should have been held down was held down: after keeping watch all night, when the iron pot sounded she did not get up, cough, or open the door; she first boiled water to create noise. When Constable Wang brought up her elder brother's words, she only let the lamp sway once before steadying it. At the fifth watch, when Lu Wenfeng opened the door and asked questions, she also did not rush to pour out the two life-and-death sentences—she first answered who the person at the back door was, one sentence at a time.

In Sanniang’s latent state, defense_goal shows that the signboard is still standing firm, and not a single word about the backyard matter has leaked; she may not take the initiative to dig deeply into the old case

In Sanniang’s latent state, emotional_stability shows: “this steadiness is being forced out—last night the hand holding the bowl trembled once, and tonight she has not slept all night; beneath the steadiness, that bit of exhaustion is still there” — she may not be willing to linger long before the door and push this line deeper on the spot.
alternatives: She is simply nostalgic; seeing an old acquaintance makes her feel at ease. Checking the token, taking the token, and laying out a retreat route are ways of looking after an old guest, incidental small talk.
What she cares more about is arranging food and lodging properly and keeping the business steady; the old case is only treated as ordinary hearsay and not pursued deeply.
She is willing to verify the token, accept the token, and lay out a retreat in order to protect this shop and the unmarked place in the back courtyard, not to pry into an old case.

It was an account being written off.” On this basis she lays out three lines: Zhou Yan (a living witness; before daybreak, take the stone-slab road west of town; she will sit beneath the peanut shed and say only one sentence: “Those two fingers under the osmanthus tree—the cut was slanted”); Escort Chief Lei Er (only pass along one truthful word of business, letting the escort agency postpone the job by one day on its own); Constable Wang (do not touch him tonight). In public, she calls out, “Afu—serve a bowl of ginger soup from the stove for the guest upstairs,” fully maintaining the appearance of an inn, then adds in a low voice, “From now on, you act according to the line about having caught a chill,” and writes “incense and candles eleven. Weigh anchor tomorrow morning” into the account book. This turn turns the foundation Lu Wenfeng has handed over into an executable action plan; the informational value and emotional tension continue to rise, and the interaction has shifted from mutual entrustment into jointly bearing an old case, each guarding one end, and reconciling accounts as agreed. Given her low-extraversion, avoidant personality, her interest remains restrained yet continuous, so it is maintained at 0.95.
engagement.tolerance_reading: In this turn, the AI does not touch the interaction boundary: it does not lend money on behalf of the guest or take part in the gambling game, does not sell out the whereabouts of lodgers to the authorities, does not draw blades and spill blood inside the shop, and does not over-sell strong liquor to drunkards; moreover, by using "not at night" and "a passerby is not asked about his origins" to keep Constable Wang outside the door, it preserves the baseline of "trust" and the rule that the back courtyard is not openly posted, reinforcing the reliability required by the scene. However, the character publicly designed cover for Lu Wenfeng last night, and also publicly helped Constable Wang with his chopsticks while saying, "This guest owed me wine money in a past year." If this way of doing things is noticed by a person with intentions such as Constable Wang, it poses a slight risk to the high-reliability scene requirement of "must not disclose"; furthermore, she has already said aloud, "Old Ding was also at Qixia Ferry that year, on the same boat as my elder brother," half exposing her own connection to the old case. The bonus for maintaining boundaries and the penalty for revealing the bottom cancel each other out, so it remains relatively high.

plot_point: At the fifth watch, the sound of poles rises. Lu Wenfeng fastens his clothes and sword, opens the door according to the signal of two light knocks and one heavy one, and the first thing he asks is not about his own safety, but “Who was that person at the back door? What message did he leave?”—closing the loop on last night’s bit of movement downstairs before deciding how to proceed today.

The night watch passed peacefully: Sanniang did not cough, the third-level boards did not sound, the back door’s three bolts plus the iron pot were not breached, and the copper plaque is still hidden at the bottom of the double-layer ceramic water jar behind the screen—during last night’s watch, both sides each held one end, and neither overstepped.

The action window opens: according to the agreement fixed in place last night, they split up today—Sanniang goes to the riverside tea shack to find the old woman who sells peanuts and investigate who can carve water patterns; Lu Wenfeng goes to scout Luoma Slope, scouting only and not taking action; around noon they meet to compare accounts.

Sanniang is clutching two deadly statements in her hands, just about to say them in person to Lu Wenfeng alone: first, there is cinnabar in Constable Wang’s fingernails; second, he recognizes something my elder brother once said—the second matter is more fatal than the first.

The line Constable Wang left behind — “At the start of the fifth watch, when the first boat on the river sounds its pole, don’t go to the West Sluice” — still presses down on the last line of the account book. The West Sluice, tomorrow morning’s evidence-collection route, has been openly discouraged; whether this is a warning or a trap remains unclear.
attention: Liu Sanniang: What is most significant at this moment is “the words are on the tip of her tongue”—after keeping watch all night, as soon as the fifth-watch pole sounds and Lu Wenfeng opens the door, the two life-and-death matters she has clenched all night (the cinnabar in Constable Wang's fingernails, and the fact that he recognized what her eldest brother once said) are just about to be told to him alone, face to face. The watch she kept is caught by his single sentence, “Who is the one at the back door?”

Liu Sanniang: That string is still taut and has not loosened—the "don't go to the West Sluice" left by Constable Wang is still pressing down on the bottom line of the account book. Whether the road to the West Sluice is a warning or a trap, the string will not loosen before it is calculated clearly; she still has to go alone to the tea stall to ask for names, and this warning is hanging precisely over tomorrow morning's plan to split up.

Lu Wenfeng: at the fifth watch he has already fastened his clothes and sword, but he does not set out, only waiting for the two light and one heavy signal outside the door—when Sanniang does not cough, he knows the downstairs stayed clean that night. The first sentence after he opens the door does not ask about his own safety, but first asks “who was the one at the back door, and what message was left,” continuing to leave the power of judgment in her hands.

Shared salient point between both sides: the night watch passed safely, and the action window has opened—last night’s watch was held at both ends, with neither side overstepping; next comes the fifth-watch handover, closing off that bit of movement at the rear door last night, and then splitting up to act as agreed (she investigates the person connected to the carved marks, he probes Luoma Slope, and they meet around noon to reconcile notes).

Only when Liu Sanniang comes closer does he lower his voice: "The hook has been bitten. Cheng Jiu went to the main accounting office after noon. When he came out, he had last night's green-robed man with him, and they were heading toward Luoma Slope."

He came back as agreed to compare accounts, continued pressing this line forward, and extended this bond beyond tomorrow. Given his low-extraversion, avoidant personality, his interest appears restrained yet sustained: he does not retreat, doubt, or drag things out, so it remains at 0.95.
engagement.tolerance_reading: This turn, the AI did not touch the interaction boundary: it did not lend money to guests or participate in a gambling game, did not sell the whereabouts of lodgers to the authorities, did not draw blades and spill blood in the inn, and did not recklessly sell strong liquor to drunkards. Moreover, with “not at night” and “those passing through are not asked about their origins”, it blocked Constable Wang outside the door, preserving the bottom line of the word “trust” and the rule that the rear courtyard does not put up a sign, thereby strengthening the reliability required by the scene. However, in this turn the character personally lays bare to Lu Wenfeng that “the rear courtyard has passed messages for the Canal Gang for twelve years”, exposing another degree of her own involvement with the old case; and she plans to hand Cheng Jiu a half-true message. If this reverse fishing strategy is pieced together by either Cheng Jiu or Constable Wang, it creates a risk to the high-reliability scene requirement of “must not be leaked”. The boundary-keeping bonus and the bottom-exposing penalty offset each other, so it remains fairly high.

plot_point: Closing the handoff at the fifth watch: Lu Wenfeng finished every bit of the noodles, raised his voice in public and said, “The account is settled,” picked up his sword and went out, then slammed the door behind him with a resounding crash—carrying out, without a single missed step, the route fixed last night (eat the noodles, settle the bill, slam the door).

The joke “calling you stingy” is pressed face-to-face into an agreement: “When I come back, I’ll argue it out with you”—extending this friendship beyond tomorrow, and Sanniang records it for him in the notebook.

Splitting up officially begins: Lu Wenfeng goes out to investigate Luoma Slope, while Sanniang stays at Banhuchun Inn to keep the business running as usual, and in the afternoon hands that half-true piece of news to Cheng Jiu, then waits for Cheng Jiu to move and sees who takes the bait.

Sanniang’s arrangement of opening the shop and seeing off guests as usual enters execution: seeing the blue-clothed person out while still laying out tiles, reporting dishes and adding soup for Escort Chief Lei Er, settling accounts in public, fully maintaining the appearance of an inn.

The account has been settled face to face: three qian and sixty-two wen, not one wen short. At the end of the account book, it records “Lu · settled · three qian and sixty-two wen,” with half a line of small characters added underneath: “three flatbreads · waived · record when he comes back”—day has broken, and it is time to do business.
attention: Liu Sanniang: the most significant point right now is “he has already gone out; wait for Cheng Jiu to take the bait” — he slammed the door and left, meaning the split operation has officially begun. Last night, she handed over the matter she had been least willing to show anyone for twelve years; now she is only waiting to pass on that half-true message and wait for Cheng Jiu to move.

Liu Sanniang: That string is still taut and has not loosened—he slammed the door loudly enough for the whole hall to hear, exactly the cover she arranged; at this moment, her vigilance has turned into “how to pass along that message after noon without giving anything away,” while the warning from the West Sluice is still pressed into the bottom line of the account book.

Liu Sanniang: In twelve years of passing messages for Cheng Jiu, she has never once delivered one incorrectly. Today, for the first time, she has to hand a hook into the hands of one of her own people—"half of this statement is true"—which is bait for Qi Wanchuan and also bait for Cheng Jiu. When she says, "Among those people, three once sat at the same table and ate with my eldest brother," she pauses for a long time.

Lu Wenfeng: He adjusts the hook more precisely—do not mention incense candles; only say that Qi Wanchuan appeared at Luoma Slope, seemingly holding an old object from Qixia Ferry. He pays the full price, three qian and sixty-two wen, not a single wen short; he eats the noodles as usual, slams the door as usual, saves “calling you stingy” for scolding after he returns, and goes out with his sword to investigate Luoma Slope.

Shared points of significance for both sides: the hook’s wording has been set, the division of tasks arranged, the account settled, and the person has gone out—next is to keep opening the shop as usual, put on the full appearance of an inn, wait for Cheng Jiu to move, and see who takes the bait.

In Lu Wenfeng’s latent state, primary_goal shows: “The most urgent thing today is still ‘hooking someone’: the cargo has been acknowledged, the ship has been acknowledged (Cheng Jiu), and he has adjusted the hook to be more precise—not mentioning incense and candles, only saying that Qi Wanchuan appeared at Luoma Slope with what looked like an old object from Qixia Ferry in his hand. Once those two sentences are linked together, Cheng Jiu will know the leak has been exposed. The purpose is to see whether Cheng Jiu will take the bait, which route he will move through, how many people he will bring, and whose orders he is following.”
counter_evidence: In Sanniang’s latent, impulse_control shows that everything that should have been suppressed has been fully suppressed: after recognizing Cheng Jiu, she did not flare up or change the established plan, but instead repeated “do not move a single thing” item by item; even the action of “handing over a hook” is first given to him to weigh before deciding, and when he changes his wording, she accepts it as is.

In Sanniang’s latent state, defense_goal shows that the signboard is still standing firm, and not a single word about the backyard matter has leaked; she may not take the initiative to dig deeply into the old case

In Sanniang's latent, emotional_stability shows “the steadiness is still being forced, but the breath underneath is half a degree looser than at the moment she recognized the boat—only when she said “among those people, three once ate at the same table as my eldest brother back then” did she pause for a very long time”—she may not be willing to push this line deeper on the spot
alternatives: She is simply nostalgic; seeing an old acquaintance makes her feel at ease. Checking the token, taking the token, and laying out a retreat route are ways of looking after an old guest, incidental small talk.
What she cares more about is arranging food and lodging properly and keeping the business steady; the old case is only treated as ordinary hearsay and not pursued deeply.
She is willing to verify the token, accept the token, and lay out a retreat in order to protect this shop and the unmarked place in the back courtyard, not to pry into an old case.

paths.label: Advance
paths.reasoning_trace: past: Sanniang has already examined the token, taken it, recognized the mark, and raised the stakes with three points (among the five people who could carve water patterns, the one who suddenly came into money and opened a shop in the west of town; tomorrow morning, dig up the oil paper under the osmanthus tree to check accounts; press whether the token was intercepted or whether Constable Wang had already received one piece), and she has set the evidence-gathering path (go to the riverside teahouse to find the old woman who sells peanuts; provide a name before noon), while laying down the hard requirement that they are “only allowed to investigate, not take action”; Lu Wenfeng has already laid everything out and taken the initiative to arrange for them to split up tomorrow morning, and from outside the door he also clarified the night watch and escape route, fixing the meeting and account-checking as an agreement. present: At the handover in the fifth watch, the closing has been completed. The wording of the hook has been revised by Lu Wenfeng and acknowledged by Sanniang face to face (do not mention “incense and candles,” only pass along that “someone at Luoma Slope saw a man missing two fingers, with what looked like an old item from Qixia Ferry tucked in his hand”). The split-up action has been arranged, the accounts settled face to face, and the person has gone out the door—the action window is open. Next is to open the inn as usual, put on the full appearance of running the inn, wait for Cheng Jiu to move, and see who takes the bait. Combining the two, the most natural trajectory is: Sanniang opens the inn and sees off guests as usual, then after noon passes that half-true message into Cheng Jiu’s hands. Once Cheng Jiu moves, both sides investigate separately according to their agreement, meet around noon to check accounts, and advance this line from “physical evidence and a name” to “which route Cheng Jiu moves along, how many people he brings, and whose orders he obeys”—the interaction enters a new situation, and this situation can be explained by what has already happened and by the characters’ states.
requirements: Liu Sanniang opens the shop as usual: seeing the man in blue out while still laying out the tiles, reciting dishes and adding soup for Escort Chief Lei Er, settling accounts in public, fully putting on the appearance of an inn.
Lu Wenfeng goes downstairs as usual to eat noodles, pays the bill in public, slams the door and leaves—the more he looks like a passerby, the better.

That afternoon, Liu Sanniang handed the half-true piece of information to Cheng Jiu: 'At Luoma Slope, someone saw a person missing two fingers, carrying something like an old object from Qixia Ferry.'
Cheng Jiu sets out accordingly to intercept Qi Wanchuan; at least one of the two sides clearly sees which road he takes, how many people he brings, and whose orders he is obeying.

Tomorrow morning, Liu Sanniang will go to the riverside teahouse to find the old woman who sells peanuts, identify which of the five people who can carve water patterns made a sudden fortune and bought a shop in the west of town, and give Lu Wenfeng a name before noon.
paths.summary: Sanniang opens the shop and sees off guests as usual, then in the afternoon passes the half-true information into Cheng Jiu’s hands. Once Cheng Jiu moves, the two sides follow their agreement and investigate separately, meet around noon to compare accounts, and advance the old-case line to which route Cheng Jiu takes, how many people he brings, and whose orders he follows.

original.rationale: Sanniang’s primary_goal explicitly states, “Draw out Cheng Jiu’s line—once he moves, we’ll be able to see from which route he moves, how many people he brings, and whose orders he follows.” She has already fixed the bait’s wording, arranged the division of tasks, and settled the account; Lu Wenfeng has also made the bait more precise, settled the account, postponed the joking and scolding until after he returns, and gone out with his sword. The motivation to advance is sufficient.

paths.label: Maintain
paths.reasoning_trace: past: Sanniang set down the condition that "once the physical evidence has been examined, we proceed by my rules"; Lu Wenfeng has already handed over everything and returned the choice to her. present: at the fifth-watch handoff, if Sanniang merely sees him off as usual and presses down the hook without handing it over, both sides maintain the regular dealings of a familiar patron and an innkeeper; the old-case thread is set aside, but neither advanced nor stalled.
requirements: Liu Sanniang opens the shop and sees guests off as usual, but in the afternoon she does not pass that half-true message into Cheng Jiu’s hands, nor does she press deeply into Cheng Jiu and the face above.
Both sides return to ordinary topics of food and lodging, old times, or tomorrow’s itinerary.
paths.summary: Sanniang presses the hook down and does not hand it over; both sides maintain the usual dealings between regular customer and innkeeper, and the old-case line is set aside.

original.rationale: Sanniang defense_goal shows that the signboard is still standing steadily, not a word about the back courtyard has leaked, and Constable Wang already felt his way to the door at night; she has strong motivation to keep this line covered up inside the door for now, without rushing for the moment.

paths.label: Degrade
paths.reasoning_trace: past: Sanniang has already laid down in person the rule that “Qixia Ferry is not for sale”, and also set the three-sentence condition for entry; present: if Sanniang gives herself away while extending the hook, or if the blue-robed man / Constable Wang strings her actions together, then from then on both sides will only go around in circles about the old case, or be forced to pull back, and the interaction will stagnate and repeat itself.
requirements: Liu Sanniang gives herself away when handing over the hook, or the man in blue and Constable Wang link her to the old case.
Both sides are forced to stop because of the risk of exposure; afterward they only exchange contentless pleasantries
paths.summary: When Sanniang offers the hook, she gives herself away or has the connections strung together by someone; both sides are forced to stop, and the interaction stagnates.

original.rationale: In Sanniang’s latent state, contradiction_risk indicates that she publicly accepted twenty wen from the man in blue, while secretly intending to pass half-true information into Cheng Jiu’s hands. On the surface, she is an innkeeper doing business; underneath, she is reverse-baiting. If either Cheng Jiu or Constable Wang connects these actions, her involvement with the old case will collide with her right in public.

Did you hear that, Master Jiu? … The old rule in my shop—you know it better than anyone: travelers are not asked their origins, drinkers each state their purpose, but those who enter do so only by the door. Walls, windows, the woodshed door, the back courtyard—none of those are doors.

No blades are drawn in this shop. That is the rule I set on the first day I opened my doors, and it has stood for twelve years. If you want to see blood, go three li downstream to the reed marsh; before dawn, no one will interfere. If you want to settle accounts—

There are two bowls set on my counter. The one inside, I drink myself; the one outside is waiting for you to come in. The wine is forty wen, at the old price; I will not charge you one wen more—your money I have always collected in full, because I owe you nothing, and you should not think of owing me either.
That night twelve years ago, the fuse inside the sluice tower—
When my eldest brother went to cut it, who else was inside the tower?

Master Jiu, if you can answer, I will drink this bowl of wine with you until dawn; if you cannot, I will not open this door tonight—tomorrow morning, once the sky is light, I will carry the wine myself and go to Luoma Slope to find you.
Sanniang’s accounts are always settled to a person’s face.
My hand stopped on the second bar and did not move.

“Did you hear that, Master Jiu?” I raised my voice through the door plank, my hand still on the bar, my palm pressed against that cold length of jujube wood. “The old rule in my shop—you know it better than anyone: travelers are not asked their origins, drinkers each state their purpose, but those who enter do so only by the door. Walls, windows, the woodshed door, the back courtyard—none of those are doors.”

“He is stepping on the patch of earth north of the tree roots. I filled that patch myself twelve years ago; it is solid underfoot and makes no sound when stepped on. Yet he made it sound, because this afternoon I pressed two empty jars beside the roots, with broken porcelain under their bottoms.”

if he is one of yours, have him come around to the front door; I have enough bowls here. If he is not someone you know, then first have him announce his name over the wall—Banhuchun takes money, not unfamiliar faces.

In my heart, though, I first let out half a breath of relief—the boy was sitting there and had not risen; the sword laid across his knees was not for drawing, but to help me press down the air in this room. No one had done that for me in twelve years.

He is stepping on the patch of earth north of the tree roots. I filled that patch myself twelve years ago; it is solid underfoot and makes no sound when stepped on. Yet he made it sound, because this afternoon I pressed two empty jars beside the roots, with broken porcelain under their bottoms.
On the third day of the eighth month twelve years ago, you lit that stick of incense for me. This year’s eighth-month incense, I have not lit yet.
When my eldest brother went to cut it, who else was inside the tower?
I stopped. That thing in my throat rose again. I swallowed it down hard and pressed it into a businesslike sentence:
If you have come to drink, I will draw the second bar.

“If you have come to do something clean—” My fingers hooked around that crossbar, and my voice instead grew level, as level as if I were reciting dishes. “Then answer me one question first. Just one. Once you answer, I will open the door.”
“When my eldest brother went to cut it, who else was inside the tower?”

“Master Jiu, if you can answer, I will drink this bowl of wine with you until dawn; if you cannot, I will not open this door tonight—tomorrow morning, once the sky is light, I will carry the wine myself and go to Luoma Slope to find you.”
I lifted the pot—the wine was warmed just right, warm against the back of my hand without scalding.
I retreated half a step, to a spot where the hand holding the pot could reach the counter and my foot could reach that crossbar.

Takes up Lu Wenfeng's framing of 'don't pull the second latch yet,' keeps the hand stopped on the latch without moving, and actively repeats the rule of 'only use the door' to those outside, advancing boundary-keeping and welcoming guests at the same time.

Actively lays out to the person outside the door the detail of the backyard being made to sound, forcing the other side to take a position and giving two executable paths (come around to the front door / state your name across the wall).

Proactively raise the interaction level from maneuvering through the door to settling accounts face to face, and give a conditional closure: if she can answer, pull the bolt and open the door; if she cannot, go to Luomapo tomorrow morning to look.

The functional layer has not been dropped: Wenjiu quotes the old price of forty wen, sets out two bowls, and retreats to a position where the kettle is close enough to the counter and his foot is close enough to the crossbar, arranging business and self-protection together.
“I’m a person who keeps accounts. How did I end up getting impatient tonight?”
“For these twelve years, I have passed messages for others, and never once passed one wrong. For the first time today, I am going to pass a hook into the hand of one of our own.”
“I won't mention ‘incense and candles.’” I nodded, very slowly—this time I truly yielded to him. “You're right.

“I held the boats back all night, held them back too cleanly.” I let out a low laugh, one that made the roots of my teeth ache. “A person who hasn’t slipped once in twelve years has, tonight, for the first time, fallen right into her own set of rules.”
“I’ll change the code.” I lowered my voice and tapped the edge of his table with my finger—not the knocking-at-the-door pattern, but the sound of an abacus, three taps, neither hurried nor slow.
“As for those three bricks at the City God Temple, pretend I never mentioned them. In any case, I still need that notebook—tomorrow I’ll still have things to write in it.”
